newsitem.title: USA: Pilot error cited in Maine oil tanker accident.
newsitem.headline: Pilot error cited in Maine oil tanker accident.

text.p: Error by a docking pilot is the apparent cause of an oil tanker accident that spilled about 170,000 gallons (4000 barrels/640,000 liters) of fuel into Portland Harbor on Friday, a federal investigator said Monday.

The pilot gave an incorrect instruction to the helmsman of the 560-foot (170-metre) tanker Julie N causing the ship to crash Friday into a drawbridge, National Transportation Safety Board representative Bill Woody told reporters.

The accident apparently occurred as the pilot, James Mooney, a 20-year veteran of the port, was attempting to correct for tricky currents in the aproach to the narrow passage through the bridge that crosses the harbor.
"The pilot freely admitted that he inadvertantly asked for a hard left when he meant a hard right," Woody told reporters.
Officials have not estimated damages from the accident which damaged the bridge and has kept the harbor partially closed to tankers and fishing boats. Cleanup operations continued Monday.

The accident is threatening a potential oil shortage for Maine and officials are considering asking the Environmental Protection Agency to temporarily lift a requirement that cars in two southern counties use a special reformulated gas to reduce air pollution.
The Liberian-registered Julie N is owned by New York-based Maritime Overseas Corp, a unit of Overseas Shipholding Group Inc. a company official said. It was chartered by Global Petroleum Corp.
